Subject: AuroraSoft — post-demo recap & initial sizing

Hi Laura — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of AuroraSoft needs
- Workload: conversational support + structured extractors (multi-turn chat).
- Current monthly baseline: ~30M input+output tokens (est); expected ~3x growth over 6–9 months to ~90M.
- Typical response size: 300–700 tokens (prompt + completion average ~550 tokens).
- Peak concurrency: ~120 concurrent active chats (spikes to ~200 for short windows).
- Latency target: 95th <= 300ms for short prompts, sub-1s for heavier completions.

Primary asks from the call
1) Dedicated reserved lanes that guarantee steady throughput and lower unit cost vs hosted.
2) Guidance on GPU family trade-offs (H100 vs A100/80GB) for latency/unit-econ.
3) Target unit price: Aurora is aiming for ~$85/1M tokens as the internal threshold (budget range discussed $8k–$25k/mo to start).
4) Pilot path: 2-week pilot to validate latency & token economics on real traffic before committing to a 3–12 month reservation.

Initial Redwood sizing ideas (need your confirmation on traffic distribution)
- Option A (latency-first): 2 x H100 reserved lane + 1 x burst lane — steady throughput ~40–55M tokens/month at target latency, estimated committed cost bracket: $18k–$28k/month.
- Option B (cost-first): 3 x A100-80GB reserved lane (quantized profile) — steady throughput ~35–50M tokens/month, estimated bracket: $12k–$20k/month, slightly higher 95p latency.
- Fallback policy: route non-latency-critical requests to quantized A100 pool during sustained peaks to keep unit cost near your $85/1M goal.

Next steps I propose
- I’ll attach a short SKU breakdown + example econ math mapping (per-1M token cost by configuration).
- Ben to share a pilot statement of work and trial onboarding checklist.
- Please confirm: target pilot start week (you mentioned late April?) and procurement contact to loop in.

Attachments: AuroraSoft-Reserved-Proposal-v1.pdf, throughput-matrix-logs.csv

Thanks — happy to calibrate numbers once you confirm realistic month-1 and month-6 token assumptions.

—
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

2) Target $85/1M is our internal stretch target; procurement will expect a mid-range option around $110/1M unless we trade a longer term commit.
3) Can you give an explicit example: for Option A (2x H100) what is the modeled $/1M at 30M and at 90M tokens? We need the delta to present to procurement.

Procurement is: Priya Natarajan <procurement@aurorasoft.com> (cc’ed). Pilot window: late April works for us — prefer Apr 26 start.

Thanks,

Thanks for the details — see the quick worked example below (ballpark modeled at current performance/quantization assumptions):

Worked example (Option A: 2x H100 reserved lanes)
- Fixed monthly reservation cost (2x H100 lanes, baseline): $22,500/month (includes burst credit and routing).
- Pilot discount: first 2 weeks on us for validation (no reservation charge for pilot).
- Estimated variable infra + infra ops at 30M tokens: ~$2,000/month additional (io, storage, logs, support), modeled total = $24,500 -> unit = $24,500 / 30 = ~$817/1M tokens.
- Estimated at 90M tokens (same reservation): $24,500 / 90 = ~$272/1M tokens.

Notes:
- Those numbers assume minimal quantization (latency-first). If we move heavier quantization and batching profiles we can push unit down ~25–40% depending on quality acceptance (this is where the A100 configuration yields better $/1M in practice).
- The large delta between 30M and 90M shows the fixed-reservation amortization effect — this is typical for reserved GPU lanes.

Action items for procurement packet
- Ben to prep a short price deck showing Option A vs Option B with modeled $/1M at 30M/60M/90M.
- Marissa to capture legal/term windows for 3mo/6mo/12mo commitments (cancellation & usage SLOs).
- Logan to set up pilot onboarding doc and a test dataset ingestion checklist.

I’ll attach the SKU breakdown and a simple excel that maps reservation count -> modeled $/1M for the three traffic tiers.

—
Logan
